whatItIs.heading: What is smoke clean-up?
whatItIs.body:
Smoke clean-up is the professional removal of smoke residue, soot, and embedded odor from a property where the structure itself is intact. It is the primary scope after a contained kitchen fire, a fireplace malfunction, or a neighboring house fire that sent smoke through your home's air gaps and HVAC system without causing direct structural damage.

Smoke clean-up is distinct from full fire damage restoration, which also involves structural demolition and rebuild. But it is not a DIY job. Smoke residue comes in three chemically different types—dry smoke from fast-burning materials, wet smoke from slow-burning plastics and rubber, and protein smoke from cooking—and each requires a different cleaning method. Using the wrong approach permanently sets staining and drives odor deeper into porous surfaces. Gallagher Restoration Co. identifies the residue type before any cleaning begins and works systematically from ceilings down, including HVAC decontamination and content restoration for salvageable items.

steps.title: Assessment and residue classification
steps.body: IICRC-trained technicians identify the fire source and classify smoke residue type across all affected rooms and the HVAC system before any cleaning begins. Dry smoke, wet smoke, and protein residue require different cleaning agents and methods. Classification determines the entire scope.

steps.title: Surface cleaning—ceilings, walls, contents
steps.body: Technicians work top-to-bottom through each affected space: ceilings, wall surfaces, exposed framing if applicable, furniture, and contents. Dry smoke responds to HEPA vacuuming and dry chemical sponges. Wet smoke and protein residue require wet chemical cleaners and enzyme treatments applied to each surface type.

steps.title: HVAC decontamination
steps.body: Smoke travels through return air ducts faster than it moves through rooms. Duct surfaces, registers, air handlers, and filters are cleaned and replaced. Skipping HVAC decontamination is the single most common reason smoke odor returns weeks after a cleanup.

steps.title: Odor elimination and content restoration
steps.body: Thermal fogging and hydroxyl generators neutralize odor molecules embedded in porous materials—drywall, insulation, upholstery, clothing. Salvageable contents including textiles, electronics, and documents are inventoried and sent to a restoration facility when on-site treatment is not sufficient.

signs.heading: Signs your home needs professional smoke clean-up
signs.intro: Smoke infiltrates spaces invisibly. By the time you smell it in a back bedroom, it has already deposited residue on every surface between the fire source and that room.

items.title: Visible soot on walls, ceilings, or surfaces
items.body: Soot is corrosive—it begins etching paint, glass, and metal within hours. The longer it sits, the more surfaces require full replacement rather than cleaning.

items.title: Smoke smell that persists after ventilation
items.body: If the odor returns after opening windows for 24 hours, it is embedded in porous materials. Ventilation alone cannot extract odor from drywall, insulation, or upholstery.

items.title: Residue on the inside of HVAC registers
items.body: Dark film on supply or return registers means smoke entered the duct system. Every time the HVAC runs, it recirculates residue and odor through the entire home.

items.title: Discoloration on ceilings near light fixtures or vents
items.body: Smoke follows air movement. Yellow or gray staining near ceiling penetrations indicates residue has deposited in the path of airflow, often beyond the primary fire room.

items.title: Health symptoms—headache, eye irritation, coughing
items.body: Unresolved smoke residue contains particulates and volatile organic compounds that continue off-gassing after the fire is extinguished. Persistent symptoms are a signal the indoor air quality has not been restored.

whyUs.heading: Why homeowners in Southern California call Gallagher for smoke clean-up
whyUs.body:
The most common mistake after a smoke event is treating it like a cleaning problem rather than a chemistry problem. Smoke residue type determines the cleaning method—and using the wrong product on wet smoke or protein residue permanently sets staining and locks odor into the substrate. Gallagher Restoration Co. has handled smoke clean-up across Southern California for more than 15 years, across every residue type and every room configuration.

The crew is IICRC-trained in fire and smoke remediation. HVAC decontamination is included in every smoke clean-up scope because skipping it is the single most common reason odor returns after the work is done. Contents—textiles, electronics, photos—are inventoried and handled through a restoration process rather than discarded without documentation. Gallagher Restoration Co. also coordinates with your insurance carrier from day one, which matters because smoke clean-up is a covered loss under most California homeowners policies. Call (951) 541-0034 and a real person answers, any hour.

pricing.heading: Smoke clean-up pricing—what to expect
pricing.body: Every smoke clean-up job starts with a free on-site assessment. Smoke clean-up in Southern California typically ranges from $1,000 to $12,000. The lower end reflects a small contained fire—a kitchen stove incident, for example—where smoke infiltration is limited to one or two rooms and residue type is dry smoke. The upper end reflects a larger footprint with wet smoke or protein residue, significant HVAC contamination, multi-room content restoration, and materials that require replacement rather than cleaning. Square footage, residue type, HVAC involvement, and content restoration scope all drive the final number. Gallagher Restoration Co. builds the documentation package your adjuster needs from the initial visit forward.

faqs.q: Can smoke damage be cleaned without replacing drywall?
faqs.a: Often yes, if the residue is dry smoke and cleaning begins within the first 24 to 48 hours. Wet smoke and protein residue penetrate drywall paper more aggressively and may require replacement even with prompt treatment. Gallagher Restoration Co. assesses whether surfaces are cleanable or need replacement during the initial site visit—there is no charge for that assessment.

faqs.q: How long does smoke odor take to go away after a fire?
faqs.a: Smoke odor that persists beyond 48 hours of ventilation will not resolve on its own. It is embedded in porous materials—drywall, insulation, flooring, upholstery. Professional treatment with thermal fogging and hydroxyl generators typically eliminates embedded odor within one to three days of treatment, depending on the extent of infiltration.

faqs.q: Does homeowners insurance cover smoke clean-up in California?
faqs.a: Yes, in most cases. Standard California homeowners policies cover smoke damage from a sudden and accidental fire event, including clean-up costs and content restoration. Gallagher Restoration Co. documents the scope from day one and coordinates directly with your adjuster so the claim process does not delay the work.

faqs.q: My neighbor's house had a fire—do I need smoke clean-up in my home?
faqs.a: Possibly. Smoke from an adjacent structure can enter your home through gaps around windows, doors, attic vents, and the HVAC system, depositing residue and odor without any visible exterior damage. If your home smells like smoke or you notice soot on interior surfaces, a professional assessment is the fastest way to determine scope.

faqs.q: What health risks are associated with fire and smoke damage?
faqs.a: Smoke and soot contain particulates and volatile organic compounds that can cause respiratory issues, eye and throat irritation, headaches, and aggravated asthma or allergies. Residue that is not fully removed continues to off-gas for weeks. Consult a healthcare professional if you experience persistent symptoms, and don't re-occupy a smoke-affected space until it has been professionally cleaned and cleared.

faqs.q: What should I do about smoke odor in my home?
faqs.a: Persistent smoke odor is embedded in porous materials—drywall, insulation, upholstery, HVAC ducts—and cannot be resolved with air fresheners or ventilation alone. Professionals use thermal fogging, hydroxyl generators, and HVAC decontamination to neutralize embedded odor at the source. Heavily affected items that cannot be treated are inventoried, documented for the claim, and replaced.
